Dwivesh Mishra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 October,
2024
Author: Maninder S. Bhatti
Bench: Maninder S. Bhatti 
 Neutral Citation No. 2024:Mphc-Jbp:51942
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur 
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Maninder S. Bhatti
 On The 17 th Of October, 2024
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 41460 of 2024
 Dwivesh Mishra
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri D.S. Dubey - Advocate for the applicant. 
 Shri C.K. Mishra - Government Advocate for the respondent/S
 Order 
This is repeat (second) bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.137/2024 dated 19.07.2024 registered at Police Station Janeh, District Rewa or the offences punishable under Sections 8, 21, 22 of NDPS Act and Section 5/13 of M.P. Drug Control Act. 
2. Earlier bail application of the present applicant was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 09.09.2024 in M.Cr.C.No.36961/2024.
3. The counsel for the applicant submits that the present applicant is a license holder issued by Food Safety and Drug Administration, Uttar Pradesh. It is contended by the counsel that the applicant had purchased 5850 bottles of Wincerex Syrup which is manufactured by Wings Pharmaceuticals Private Limited Delhi and then the entire bottles were intended to sold to retailers. Therefore, the allegations of seizure of the aforesaid bottles from the possession of the present applicant is unsustainable and accordingly, the present applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail. 
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposed the said NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:51942 2 MCRC-41460-2024 prayer and submitted that there is seizure of huge quantity of cough syrup and there is complete failure on the part of the present applicant to Dwivesh Mishra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157795556/
1 demonstrate that as to how he came in possession of the huge quantity of alleged contraband. 
Therefore, considering the role of the present applicant, application filed by the present applicant deserves to be dismissed. 
5. Heard the submissions advanced on behalf of the parties and perused the case diary.
6. A perusal of record reflects that there is no documents on record to demonstrate that the applicant had purchased 5850 bottles of Wincerex Syrup batch No. WCCS-3150 from Wings Pharmaceuticals Private Limited Delhi and this aspect has also been considered by the Special Judge while dismissing the application filed by the present applicant. It is evident that earlier bail application of the present applicant filed before this Court was dismissed as withdrawn after lengthy arguments vide order dated 09.09.2024 in M.Cr.C.No.36961/2024.
7. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and also looking to the huge quantity of contraband, it would not be appropriate to release the applicant on bail, at this stage,
inasmuch as there is no change in circumstances. 
8. Accordingly, the bail application of the applicant filed under Section 483 of BNSS stands dismissed. 
(MANINDER S. BHATTI) JUDGE sp Dwivesh Mishra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157795556/
2
